lines.name: Splinter

lines.desc: Its harpoons split in 2 at their first hit.

lines.name: Drag Line

lines.desc: Where the beam hits, its light stays for 1s and hits enemies in it.

specials.desc: While standing still, it flashes twice as fast and reaches 50% farther.

specials.desc: The far half of the beam deals 70% more damage.

deed.text: Kill 3 enemies with one flash, 150 times

lines.name: Flashover

specials.desc: Every 3s while you keep moving, a line of burning oil spills behind you, dealing 30% more damage than a pool.

specials.name: Clinging Fire
specials.desc: Its pools last 60% longer, and enemies burning in them pass their fire to those they bump into.

lines.name: Arc
lines.desc: Hits chain to 3 nearby enemies.

lines.name: Tall Rod

specials.name: Lightning Wire
specials.desc: No rod: strikes fall close around you, twice as often.

deed.text: Kill 3 enemies with one volley, 150 times

lines.desc: Flames also set enemies they touch burning for 2s.

lines.desc: Flames deal 40% more damage to rotting enemies.

specials.name: Soul Lantern
specials.desc: Gains +4% Damage for each minute held, up to +50%.

lines.desc: Spouts deal 40% more damage to frozen enemies.

specials.desc: Puddles last twice as long. A puddle with an enemy in it stops drying, up to 3 times its normal time.

lines.desc: Picks deal 40% more damage to slowed enemies.

lines.desc: Picks slow enemies they hit by 50% for 3s.

specials.desc: A pick that comes back flies out once more, at 50% damage.

lines.desc: Lost enemies stay lost 1.5s longer.

lines.desc: Two lost enemies that walk into each other are both stunned for 1s.

specials.name: Gale Note
specials.desc: The note sounds all round you and knocks enemies back twice as far.

specials.name: Rolling Fog
specials.desc: The note goes twice as far, slowly, and enemies it hits stay lost 1s longer.

weapons.name: Eel Pot

lines.desc: Bites leave rotting ground.

lines.desc: An eel pulls the enemy it bites a little way back toward its pot.

lines.name: Weak Point
lines.desc: Eels deal 40% more damage to rotting enemies.

specials.desc: Stopping after a walk sets a pot there, and every pot lunges at once. At most once every 3s.

specials.desc: A great eel lives in each pot. Once every 2s it bites an enemy right next to the pot for 2x damage and stuns it.

lines.desc: Every enemy the anchor hits takes 25% more damage for 4s, stunned or not.

lines.desc: Hits chain to 2 nearby enemies.

lines.desc: An enemy the anchor knocks back stuns the first enemy it lands on for 0.6s.

specials.desc: The longer you keep moving, the faster it swings and the more damage it deals, up to 2x each. It resets when you stop.

specials.desc: Enemies it knocks back damage the enemies they land on.

deed.text: Kill 300 enemies close beside you with it

lines.name: Splinter
lines.desc: Its pieces split in 2 at their first hit.

lines.desc: Cuts set enemies burning for 2s.

lines.name: Glass Dust
lines.desc: A piece that breaks leaves glass dust for 2s that cuts enemies walking through it.

specials.name: Well-Trodden
specials.desc: While moving, it drops glass 40% faster. Glass walked back over deals 40% more damage each time, up to 4 times.

specials.desc: Her lanterns deal the same damage as her light, not 60%, and each lasts until 3 more are set down.

lines.desc: Each pull brings in the 2 nearest enemies too.

specials.name: Whaler's Brace

specials.name: Ring of Hooks
specials.desc: Every 5s the Grapnel hooks the 3 nearest enemies and pulls them in.

lines.desc: A sweep slows enemies it hits by 30% for 2s.

lines.desc: A sweep readies the jab at once.

specials.desc: At full Momentum he jabs twice as fast.

specials.name: Crow's Landing
specials.desc: A sweep among 6 or more enemies sweeps twice.

lines.desc: Enemies a hand held are slowed by 40% for 2.5s after.

lines.desc: A grasp also reaches for the nearest enemy beside it, once every 0.5s.

specials.desc: Her thralls stay near her and bite enemies that come close, twice as fast.

specials.name: Pallbearers
specials.desc: A hit that would hurt her falls on her nearest thrall instead, once every 6s.

lines.desc: A finished enemy chills enemies near it: slowed by 30% for 2s.

lines.desc: Every 3s it throws all its pennies at once.

specials.desc: Pennies deal 50% more damage close to him, and a penny that lands close puts 2 in the purse.

lines.name: Shock
lines.desc: The flood stuns enemies it hits for 0.5s.

specials.desc: Each flood is followed 1.5s later by a second at 50% damage.

specials.name: Full Moon
specials.desc: The ebb reaches twice as far, and the flood deals 2x damage to enemies right next to her.

options.desc: With each grasp, a hand also rises beside each of her thralls, up to 3.

options.desc: Where a hand grabs, the mire churns for 1.5s, dealing 4% of the hand's damage to enemies in it every 0.5s.

options.name: Deep Hold
options.desc: Hands stun for 1.5s and squeeze for 25% of their damage every 0.5s. Rotting enemies take 50% more damage, not 25%.

options.name: Bog Kin
options.desc: Her thralls last 60% longer, and their bites rot: enemies take 25% more damage for 3s.

options.name: Bog Fire
options.desc: A thrall that dies bursts into rot, damaging enemies near it.

options.name: Full Purse
options.desc: +1 Penny for each sea chest he has brought up.

options.name: Paid in Advance
options.desc: Each crate he brings up adds 8% to the pennies' damage for the run, up to 15 crates.

options.name: Heads or Tails
options.desc: Every 2nd penny that hits strikes again for the same damage.

options.name: Paid Passage
options.desc: Pennies pass through every enemy, and he throws 2 more.

options.name: Pennies on the Eyes
options.desc: His pennies finish enemies under 30% HP, and each penny also hits the enemy beside its target for 50% damage.

options.name: Weighed Down
options.desc: Each penny on an enemy slows it by 12% and makes it take 12% more damage, up to 5 pennies.

options.name: Tide Table
options.desc: Each enemy the flood hits brings the next flood 0.1s sooner, up to 33% sooner.

options.name: Spring and Neap
options.desc: Every other flood deals 2x damage and reaches 50% farther.

options.name: Spring Tide
options.desc: A thin flood also runs out the way she faces, twice as far as the round one, and back.

options.name: Neap Pull
options.desc: The ebb pulls from twice as far and holds the enemies it pulls for 0.5s.

options.name: High Water Mark
options.desc: Where the flood passes it leaves pools that slow enemies by 30%.

options.name: Drowning Tide
options.desc: Enemies the ebb pulls take 100% more damage until the next flood.
options.price: The ebb itself does no damage

keystone.desc: An enemy that dies burning sets the nearest enemy burning.
An enemy hit by a Light weapon takes 10% more damage for 2s.

passives.name: Ballast
passives.desc: +1 Pierce and +12% Knockback (Steel). Gains Damage as it levels.

keystone.desc: Steel weapons deal 25% more damage to elites and bosses.

passives.name: Undertow
passives.desc: +1 Projectile (Sea). Gains Damage and Duration as it levels.

keystone.desc: Sea hits slow enemies by 20% for 1.5s.
After 2s of moving without a stop, each weapon's next hit is a critical hit. At most once every 2s for each weapon.

passives.name: Thick Coat
passives.desc: +15 Max HP per level. +1 Armor at Lv 3 and Lv 5.

keystone.desc: Taking a hit knocks back enemies close to you.
Opening a chest pulls in every gem on the map.
While you stand still, weapons fire 12% faster.

passives.name: Hoarfrost
passives.desc: +10% Damage and +10% Duration (Frost) per level. Frost statuses last longer too.

passives.name: Copper Wire
passives.desc: +1 Chain every other level. +8% Damage (Light) on the levels between.

keystone.desc: The last hit of a chain bursts.
An enemy that dies rotting leaves a patch of rot for 2s.

passives.name: Bittern's Call
passives.desc: +10% Area (Echo) per level. +1 Projectile (Echo) at Lv 3 and Lv 5.

keystone.desc: Every 4th volley of an Echo weapon fires again at once.

passives.name: Waders
passives.desc: +4% Move Speed and +8% Area (Frost) per level.

keystone.desc: Stand still for 1s and enemies close to you are stunned for 1s. At most once every 4s.

passives.name: Lucky Knot
passives.desc: +12% Luck per level. More drops, more Reliquaries, and fuller chests.

keystone.desc: Killing an elite has a 1 in 4 chance to give a Reroll.

relics.name: Gull Feather
relics.desc: +8% Move Speed.

relics.name: Brass Button
relics.desc: +6% Damage.

relics.name: Spark Flint
relics.desc: Every 4s while moving, a burst of sparks goes off underfoot.

relics.name: Ship's Clock
relics.desc: Every 45s, a wave knocks back nearby enemies.

relics.name: Dead Calm
relics.desc: Kills made while standing still drop double XP.

relics.name: Glass Lantern
relics.desc: Healing becomes a shield instead, up to 50% of Max HP.

relics.name: Barnacle Shell
relics.desc: Taking a hit sends out a wave that knocks enemies back. Once every 6s.

relics.name: Bloodied Hook
relics.desc: While 15 or more enemies are close, +30% Damage.

relics.name: Seventh Bell
relics.desc: Every 7th level-up gives an Ember. -10% XP Gain.

relics.name: Volatile Gems
relics.desc: XP gems explode when collected. -25% Pickup Range.

relics.name: Wreck Lantern
relics.desc: Every 2s, burning oil spills under the nearest enemy.

relics.name: Drowned Bell
relics.desc: Every 6s, the bell tolls and hits enemies near you for 40 damage. -10% Move Speed.

relics.name: Sea Urchin
relics.desc: Enemies that hit you take damage: 6 for each point of Armor.

relics.name: Quench Bucket
relics.desc: A Sea or Frost hit on a burning enemy puts the fire out. The rest of the burn hits at once, on it and the enemies touching it.

relics.name: Cold Iron
relics.desc: A Steel kill on a slowed or frozen enemy shatters it into 4 shards that slow enemies they hit.

relics.name: Watchman's Rattle
relics.desc: When 15 or more enemies have been close for 2s, every weapon fires at once. Again once the crowd drops under 8.

relics.name: Try-Pot
relics.desc: After a skip, the next level-up offers only things you own, and the one you pick gains 2 levels.

relics.name: Brine Vat
relics.desc: Slows add together, up to 80%. An enemy slowed 80% for 1s turns to salt for 4s, then dies (not bosses or captains). -15 Max HP.

relics.name: Bog Torc
relics.desc: Once a run, instead of dying: for 4s nothing can hurt you and enemies that touch you rot. Then you get up at 40% HP.

relics.name: Moon Pull
relics.desc: Every 60s, every gem on the map flies to you.

relics.name: Sea Rite
relics.desc: Kills by Sea weapons heal you 1 HP, up to 3 a second.

relics.name: Kindling
relics.desc: Elites drop an Ember twice as often, and bosses drop 2.

relics.name: Glassblower
relics.desc: Relics are offered one rarity higher. -15% Max HP.

relics.name: Gleaner's Sack
relics.desc: Every 30s, every gem on the map flies to you. -10% Damage.

relics.name: Tarred
relics.desc: Hits coat enemies in tar for 4s. A hit from another weapon bursts the tar, for 50% of the hit that put it there.

relics.name: Marsh Fever
relics.desc: Hits give a fever for 3s: the enemy takes 10% more damage. A fevered enemy passes its burn, rot, and slow to one it bumps into.

relics.name: Whetstone
relics.desc: Every 2nd level-up of a weapon is Rare or better, not every 3rd.

relics.name: Stern Lantern
relics.desc: Hits on enemies behind you deal 25% more damage.

relics.name: Stray Light
relics.desc: Final Form goals count double.

relics.name: Salt Ledger
relics.desc: Every chest from an elite or a boss also gives a Reroll.

characters.name: Lamplighter
characters.who: Lights the harbor's lamps, and carries one that burns enemies.
characters.desc: Her Lamplight burns enemies near her. With 5 or more enemies in it, she gains a spare flame every 5s, up to 3.
characters.gives: Lamps light the moment she reaches them. Lighting a lamp fills her spare flames and refills her Fuel. Each spare flame gives Lamplight +15% Damage, and +15% Area while she moves (+5% while she stands). Each lamp she lights leaves a lantern by it. While her light is dimmed, she also sets down a lantern every 30s. A lantern lasts 60s, burns enemies in its light at 60% of Lamplight's damage, and gives Lamplight +10% Damage while it stands. Lighting every lamp gets her 2 Lantern Nights ready. On the Salt Marsh her light has +50% Area, her Fuel lasts twice as long, and spare flames fill twice as fast.
characters.costs: Her light runs on Fuel. Away from lit lamps her Fuel lasts 60s, then her light dims over 30s, down to 60% Area and Damage, and her Pickup Range to 60%. Standing in a lit lamp's light refills it.

card.does: Her lamp burns enemies in its light.
card.costs: Her light dims when her Fuel runs out.

characters.name: Harpooner
characters.who: A whaler from the harbor's last crew. She fights best in the middle of the crowd.
characters.desc: Her Grapnel and chains pull enemies in and stun them, and she gains Armor for each enemy close by.

trade.deedText: Pull in 6 elites with her hook

characters.gives: Every 6s her hook flies the way she faces. It pulls in an elite or a chest, or calls the Ferryman to a mooring post. Her Grapnel deals 50% more damage to bosses. On the Salt Marsh her hook reaches twice as far for an elite, and her Grapnel gets +30% Damage.
characters.costs: She takes 20% more damage. Her Grapnel and chains pull enemies close, so she is always in the crowd.

card.does: Her Grapnel and chains pull in and stun enemies.

characters.hubLine: Tide's turning. Say the word and I'll head out.

characters.name: Punter
characters.who: A marsh boatman. He hits hardest while he keeps moving in a straight line.
characters.desc: Running straight builds Momentum: up to +40% Damage and +16% Punt Pole Area. At full Momentum the pole sweeps all around him every 3s.
characters.gives: Each step of Momentum gives his Glass Caltrops -15% Cooldown. He can cross water for 5s at a time. Enemies on foot can't follow him there. Pushing off from the water fills his Momentum. A floating chest comes out on the water for him, 1 each act. On the Salt Marsh one comes about every 5 minutes of high water instead, and each sweep counts twice toward Punt Pole's next level.
characters.costs: A sharp turn loses 1 step of Momentum. Taking a hit loses 50% of it. Stopping loses all of it. With no Momentum his weapons deal 25% less damage. 95 Max HP.

card.does: Straight runs build Momentum: up to +40% Damage.
card.costs: Turns, hits, and stops lose Momentum.

characters.hubLine: Water's low today. I can still get you up the creeks.

characters.name: Bog Warden
characters.who: She tends the dead buried in the marsh peat.
characters.desc: Enemies that die rotting, or in the grip of her Bog Hands, rise and fight for her. They deal more damage as Bog Hands levels up.
characters.gives: Walking over an enemy within 5s of its death raises it as a thrall. Bog bodies and wreck crews on the map rise when she reaches them. Each thrall gives her 1 Armor, up to 6. On the Salt Marsh, only she can raise the dead on the Drowned Causeway.
characters.costs: Her weapons other than Bog Hands deal 10% less damage.

card.does: Enemies dying in her grip rise to fight for her.
card.costs: Her other weapons deal 10% less damage.

characters.hubLine: Peat keeps a body for a hundred years. I've dug up older.

characters.name: Drowned Man
characters.who: Drowned off the breakwater and came back. He collects pennies to raise sunken crates.
characters.desc: His Grave Pennies finish ordinary enemies under 15% HP. Each penny that lands close to him pays into his purse.
characters.gives: His pennies deal more damage the fuller his purse: +30% when full. A full purse marks a sunken crate nearby, and walking to it brings it up. The map's sunken crates come up when he reaches them. Every 3rd crate is a sea chest. The first gives back 1 weapon slot, with a weapon in it. Later ones give Grave Pennies 1 level. His pennies deal 40% more damage to bosses.
characters.costs: Starts with 2 fewer weapon slots. Sea chests give back only 1 of them. 85 Max HP, -15% Move Speed.

card.does: His pennies finish enemies under 15% HP.
card.costs: 2 fewer weapon slots, 85 Max HP, -15% Move Speed.

characters.find: Something has washed up at Breakwater Point, on the Drowned Docks after the first boss.
characters.hubLine: Sea gave me back. Didn't say why.

characters.name: Tide Priest
characters.who: The Chapel's priest. She times the floods, and her attack goes off every 30s.
characters.desc: Every 30s her King Tide floods and knocks enemies back. Halfway between floods, the ebb pulls enemies toward her.

trade.deedText: Hit 20 or more enemies with one flood, 8 times

characters.gives: With 12 enemies close to her in the 5s before a flood or ebb, it comes early with +30% Damage. Each enemy a flood hits gives the next one +1.5% Damage, up to +75%. Her flood deals 50% more damage to rotting enemies. Fog Bells ring twice for her.
characters.costs: Can't heal. Each flood gives her a shield, and nothing else refills it. With no shield she takes 15% more damage. +30 Max HP.

card.does: Floods knock enemies back, and ebbs pull them in.
card.costs: Can't heal. Takes 15% more damage with no shield.

characters.find: Brother Hale at the Chapel posts a Harbor Order for her.
characters.hubLine: Thirty seconds between floods. I count them in my sleep.

enemies.name: Drowned Sailor
enemies.desc: A drowned sailor. Walks straight at you.

enemies.name: Gull
enemies.desc: A fog-sick gull. Fast, comes in flocks, and dies to one hit.

enemies.name: Mud Crab
enemies.desc: Winds up, then runs at you.

enemies.name: Bloater
enemies.desc: Bursts into rats when it dies.

enemies.name: Bilge Rat
enemies.desc: Fast and weak. Comes in packs, and pounces once when close.

enemies.name: Lantern Eater
enemies.desc: Spits pools of black water. Watch the rings.

enemies.name: Wreck Gunner
enemies.desc: Lobs slow cannonballs. Easy to see coming.

enemies.name: Drowned Bosun
enemies.desc: A big drowned sailor. Slow, and takes many hits.

enemies.name: The Harbor Maw
enemies.desc: The first boss on the Drowned Docks. It lures, slams, calls up its crew, and charges.

enemies.name: The Tidecaller
enemies.desc: The last boss on the Drowned Docks. It sends a line of water, fans of shots, and pools, then slams and charges.

enemies.name: Midge Cloud
enemies.desc: A clump of biting midges. They drift at you in threes and dart in once when close. Each bite slows you a little.

enemies.name: Salted Dead
enemies.desc: Drowned in the marsh and crusted with salt. Frost, Sea, and Steel crack the crust.

enemies.name: Mire Toad
enemies.desc: Hops at you. A ring shows where it will land.

enemies.name: Creek Eel
enemies.desc: Waits in the high water and lunges along a line as you pass, a short way onto the bank.

enemies.name: Leech
enemies.desc: Swims the creeks. Latches on and drains 1 HP every 2s. A dash throws it off.

enemies.name: Well Warden
enemies.desc: Guards the Salt Well. Throws up walls of salt.

enemies.name: The Old Grey
enemies.desc: A giant heron that stabs and leaps. When it lands on mud it gets stuck for a moment. Hit it then.

enemies.name: The Salt Widow
enemies.desc: The last boss on the Salt Marsh. She sends lightning marching in a line and throws salt shards.

buildings.desc: The harbor's big lamp. Each level pushes the fog back and opens new Harbor upgrades, bought here with materials, for every run. Two of its levels add a weapon slot to your runs.

buildings.name: Library
buildings.desc: Pay materials to start a research project. It finishes after a few runs, and what it finds (new weapons, passives, and relics) can then turn up in your runs.

buildings.name: Tavern
buildings.desc: Keeps the Harbor Orders board (goals the townsfolk post) and each character's mastery. Its later levels add relics to your runs and let a run set out with an Heirloom.

buildings.name: Docks

buildings.name: Market

buildings.name: Apothecary

buildings.name: Cartographer
buildings.desc: Draws more onto your minimap: Reliquaries wherever they drop, then small secrets, then the big ones, with hints. It also posts Challenge runs on the Harbor Orders board and opens short runs.

buildings.name: Lighthouse
buildings.desc: The old light on the point. Relight it stage by stage with materials from every map. Each stage shows on the tower and opens something new.

research.name: Stern Lines
research.desc: A pilot's notes on what to hang off the stern.

research.name: Weatherglass

research.name: Volatile Salts

research.name: Corpse Lights

research.name: Smith's Ledger

research.name: Compass Rose
research.desc: Instrument makers' drawings: compasses and rings.

research.name: Moon Tables
research.desc: Tables of high and low water.

research.name: Deep Salvage
research.desc: A diver's log of what the wrecks still hold.

research.desc: Prayers the chapel said for the drowned.

research.name: Brine Notes

research.desc: A bird hunter's notebook of calls and lamp oil.

research.desc: Notes on fog horns and lightning rods.

research.name: Anchor Smithing

research.name: Salting Ledger
research.desc: The salt house's account book.

research.name: Lantern Lore

npcs.name: Old Wick
npcs.desc: Lit the harbor's lamps for 40 years, until the fog came.

lines.text: Forty years I lit these streets. Nice to have help.
Boats at the pier again. I keep counting them.
Silas says you read everything twice. Good habit.
The fog backs off from a steady flame. Keep it fed.
Tide 5 on the docks. I lit those lamps in worse, but not by much.
Somebody lit the keeper's room on the point. First time in years.
The lighthouse is lit. I'll stick to the streets.
Half these pages are too wet to read. The rest are worth drying.
Pell keeps a tally of what you kill. I keep a tally of Pell.
Bring me more Drowned Pages. The wettest ones have the best stories.
You found what was in the wreck's hold. Pell will say he told you.
The causeway goes somewhere after all. I owe Pell a drink.
A hundred runs. The codex is twice as thick as when you started.
Sit anywhere. Most of the chairs have legs now.
Moss sends people here after her salves. I send them back.
Sailors started coming back once the lamps were lit.
The Tidecaller's bell has stopped. Drinks are on you.
The Salt Widow's dead. Half the bar claims they saw it.
Fifty runs. The board out back is your fault, you know.
The Ferryman pays in favors. I take them.
Fenn buys the Pearls you bring back. Don't tell the Ferryman.
Every hull here floats now. I patched three this week.
The drowned fellow sleeps in the boathouse. He drips on everything.
The Ferryman asked after you. He never asks after anyone.
Tide 5 on the marsh. I'd have rowed the other way.
Bring iron. I can make most things out of most things.
Hale asked me for a bell. I made him a louder one.
Six slots. Wear them all or the work was for nothing.
Three Forms on one weapon. Show me, but don't point it at the forge.
I cut the lens frame for the lighthouse. Fit on the first try.
The tide comes higher every time you ask it to.
The Tide Priest came by boat. She won't take food. Says she fasts on flood days.
The big lamp burns all night now. I sleep worse and pray less.
Tide 10 is the last one the chapel can call.
Tide 10 cleared. I rang the chapel bell for it.
Both maps at Tide 10. There's no Tide 11, so don't ask.
A bad trade beats no trade when you're short of Timber.
Hob wants iron and pays in iron. I'm working on it.
Pearls are no use to me. I buy them anyway, for Coin.
Three hundred Pearls at once. Next time bring them here.
The light ate a whole year's oil. I sold it the oil.
Drink it before you go out. Not after.
Bring me a rat's tail and I'll stop asking where you got it.
Three bottles a run. More and you rattle.
You crossed the whole marsh. Sit down and let me see your feet.
The Old Grey's gone quiet. The frogs are louder now.
The docks are bigger than they look. Check the corners.
Silas copies my charts and gets the coast wrong. On purpose, I think.
I marked the wreck. Don't say I gave it away.
The causeway was on my chart the whole time. I drew it in the wrong place.
A hundred runs, and my charts still have blank bits. Keep looking.

npcs.name: Maren
npcs.desc: Kept the light on the point before the fog.

lines.text: Glass in the lantern room again. I keep cleaning it anyway.
The gallery holds. I walked it twice to be sure.
Rang the fog bell at noon. Half the town came to look.
She's lit. Ships could find us now, if there were any.

skills.name: Great Lamp
skills.desc: Standing still, she spends a spare flame to set down a lantern for 30s. It gives Lamplight +30% Damage, not +15%.

skills.name: Lamp Row
skills.desc: Each lantern lasts until 4 more are set down, and a line of light joins each to the next, burning enemies that cross it.

skills.name: Bonfire
skills.desc: Standing still for 2s, her lamp throws a ring of fire outward every 3s.

skills.name: Lamplit Road
skills.desc: Inside a lantern's light she walks 25% faster, and her Fuel refills.

skills.name: Spare Fuel
skills.desc: When her Fuel runs out, a flask refills it once. Lighting a lamp refills the flask.

skills.name: Burn Low
skills.desc: Her light never dims. With no Fuel left it goes out for 1s in every 5s instead.

skills.name: Moth Light
skills.desc: Every 6s, enemies in her light are stunned for 0.5s.

skills.name: Signal Lamp
skills.desc: Every 8s her lamp throws a beam the way she faces, dealing 3x her light's damage to enemies along it.

skills.name: Burning Lamps
skills.desc: Lamps she has lit also burn enemies in their light, at 50% of her light's damage.

skills.name: Keeper's Vigil
skills.desc: While she stands in a lit lamp's light, her own light reaches as far as the lamp's.

skills.name: Flare Up
skills.desc: Touching a lamp she has lit sets off a burst from it that knocks enemies back. Each lamp can do it once every 30s.

skills.name: Night Watch
skills.desc: A ready Lantern Night starts when she stands in a lit lamp's light for 2s, not when a crowd comes.

skills.name: First Flame
skills.desc: She starts with 3 spare flames, and a boss's death fills them.

skills.name: Sleigh Ride
skills.desc: When her hook pulls an elite, she is pulled to it instead, hitting enemies on the way.

skills.name: Deadweight
skills.desc: Enemies the Grapnel pulls fly past her and burst where they land, damaging enemies near them.

skills.name: Boarding Action
skills.desc: After Sleigh Ride pulls her to an elite, enemies close by are stunned for 1.5s and she gets full Armor for 3s.

skills.name: Wrecking Ball
skills.desc: A pulled elite is swung once round her before it lands, hitting enemies it passes.

skills.name: Hand Line
skills.desc: Her hook flies every 3s, at 50% Range.

skills.name: Gaff Hand
skills.desc: Her hook flies twice as far and hits enemies along its line, every 9s.

skills.name: Salvager
skills.desc: Her hook pulls in every pickup she faces from across the screen, and pulling in an elite pulls every gem on the map to her, once every 30s.

skills.name: Big Game
skills.desc: A pulled elite that dies within 4s drops a second chest, and muster captains can be pulled in too.

skills.name: Barbed Hook
skills.desc: Every enemy she pulls in is hooked: it takes 30% more damage for 4s.

skills.name: Coil
skills.desc: While an elite she pulled in is stunned at her side, the Grapnel throws 50% faster.

skills.name: Bulwark
skills.desc: At 10 Armor from enemies close by, she knocks back enemies close to her and deals 12 damage, once every 8s.

skills.name: Slack Line
skills.desc: Her other chain weapons no longer pull enemies in. They knock them back, as they do for other characters.

skills.name: Ferryman's Friend
skills.desc: A post she hooks brings the Ferryman with one more thing in stock.

skills.name: Water Born
skills.desc: He crosses water for 15s, not 5s. At full Momentum on land his wake slows enemies by 50% and deals 1.6x Punt Pole's damage every 0.5s.

skills.name: Pole Vault
skills.desc: At full Momentum, running into 4 or more enemies makes him leap over them and land past them in a sweep, once every 3s.

skills.name: Cold Wake
skills.desc: Enemies that cross his wake are frozen for 1s.

skills.name: Long Jump
skills.desc: A leap carries him twice as far, and enemies he passes over are stunned for 1s.

skills.name: Dig In
skills.desc: After standing still for 1s, he loses no Damage for having no Momentum, and the pole gets +100% Area until he moves.

skills.name: Never Stop
skills.desc: At full Momentum nothing slows him, and the first enemy to touch him is knocked back and does him no harm, once every 3s.

skills.name: Slick Water
skills.desc: When he comes off the water the bank stays slick for 5s. Enemies that cross it are slowed by 50%.

skills.name: Second Chest
skills.desc: A second floating chest comes out each time.

skills.name: Pole Guard
skills.desc: A hit taken at full Momentum empties his Momentum and does no damage, once every 20s.

skills.name: Counterpoise
skills.desc: When Pole Guard goes off, the pole sweeps.

skills.name: Sculling
skills.desc: On the water he jabs twice as fast.

skills.name: Gather Way
skills.desc: Every 4th sweep that hits 3 or more fills his Momentum, once every 20s.

skills.name: Low Bridge
skills.desc: His Momentum never drops below 1 step, so his weapons never take the -25% Damage for having none.

skills.name: Barrow Keeper
skills.desc: One thrall that never expires. It gives her +6 Armor and bites all enemies near it each 1s. Each enemy that would rise adds +35% Damage.

skills.name: Great Host
skills.desc: Twice as many thralls at once, each lasting half as long.

skills.name: Keeper's Leap
skills.desc: Every 8s her Barrow Keeper thrall leaps into the biggest group near her. Enemies where it lands rot: they take 25% more damage for 3s.

skills.name: Bone March
skills.desc: Every 8s her thralls charge the way she faces, biting enemies they pass.

skills.name: Grave Goods
skills.desc: Her other weapons deal full damage while she has no thralls.

skills.name: Borrowed Hands
skills.desc: Enemies killed by her other weapons also rise, rotting or not. Those weapons deal another 10% less damage.

skills.name: Old Dead
skills.desc: Bog bodies and wreck crews last 2 minutes and follow her.

skills.name: Fresh Graves
skills.desc: Elite thralls don't count toward her 6 thralls, and last twice as long.

skills.name: Death Rattle
skills.desc: A thrall whose time is up bursts, dealing 3x its bite damage to enemies near it.

skills.name: Second Burial
skills.desc: A thrall that dies rises once more, for 50% of the time.

skills.name: Deep Barrow
skills.desc: Her thralls last 40% longer.

skills.name: Rot Walk
skills.desc: While she has 3 or more thralls, she leaves rot where she walks.

skills.name: Warden's Rest
skills.desc: While she stands still her thralls gather round her and attack twice as fast.

skills.name: Empty Hands
skills.desc: Sea chests never give back a weapon slot. Each one gives Grave Pennies 3 levels and +1 Projectile instead.

skills.name: Wrecker's Hoard
skills.desc: Sea chests give back both missing weapon slots instead of 1.

skills.name: King's Coin
skills.desc: Grave Pennies gains +5% Damage each minute of the run, up to +100%.

skills.name: Fleet
skills.desc: The purse needs 2 fewer pennies for each weapon he carries past two.

skills.name: Far Wrecks
skills.desc: His crates are marked farther out, most of a screen away, and each holds two items.

skills.name: Wash Up
skills.desc: A full purse brings the crate up at his feet, with no walk, but the purse needs 5 more pennies.

skills.name: Old Debts
skills.desc: Killing a boss fills the purse, and the crate it marks is a sea chest.

skills.name: Wreck Diver
skills.desc: The map's sunken crates hold as much as a boss's chest.

skills.name: Heavy Purse
skills.desc: The purse gives Armor as it fills, up to +5 Armor when full. Bringing up a crate empties it.

skills.name: Last Coin
skills.desc: Once a run, a blow that would kill him with a full purse empties it instead and leaves him at 30% HP.

skills.name: Cold Hands
skills.desc: When a penny finishes an enemy, enemies near it are frozen for 1s, once every 2s.

skills.name: Charon's Change
skills.desc: A penny that lands anywhere on screen pays into the purse.

skills.name: Salvage Rights
skills.desc: Reaching one of the map's sunken crates fills the purse.

skills.name: Neap Priest
skills.desc: Floods come 4 times as often, at 33% damage. Each leaves a shield of at most 8. 6 enemies close to her bring one early, not 12.

skills.name: One Great Tide
skills.desc: One flood every 45s. Deep water stays round her for 10s, slowing enemies by 50% and dealing 25% of its damage every 0.5s. +50% Damage.

skills.name: Drawdown
skills.desc: Her ebbs hold the enemies they pull for 0.6s.

skills.name: Bell Floods
skills.desc: The flood also rolls out from every Fog Bell rung this run.

skills.name: Blood Tide
skills.desc: Her floods heal her: 1 HP for every 2 enemies hit, up to 25. She gets no shield, and no longer takes 15% more damage without one.

skills.name: Sea's Armor
skills.desc: The shield each flood gives her is 50% bigger, and so is its cap.

skills.name: Slack Water
skills.desc: When her flood or ebb comes early, it stuns the enemies it hits for 3s, and the next one comes 3s later.

skills.name: Ride the Tide
skills.desc: When her flood comes early, it carries her a short distance in the direction she faces. Nothing can hurt her while it does.

skills.name: Wrack Line
skills.desc: The flood's edge leaves a line for 6s that slows enemies crossing it by 40%.

skills.name: Ebb Walk
skills.desc: For 3s after an ebb she moves 30% faster.

skills.name: Bell Call
skills.desc: A Fog Bell she has rung twice brings her flood at once.

skills.name: Stillness
skills.desc: For each 10 enemies a flood hits she gains 1 Armor for 5s, up to 5.

skills.name: Last Rites
skills.desc: Once a run, under 15% HP, the flood comes at once and she can't be hurt for 2s.

glossary.name: Run
glossary.desc: One trip out from the harbor, 20 minutes long. Bosses come at 10:00 and 20:00. Killing the last one clears the map. Whatever happens, what you found comes home.
glossary.where: Start one at the gate on the quay, or with Start run from the harbor's menu.

glossary.name: XP gems
glossary.desc: Blue gems enemies drop. Picking them up fills the bar at the top. A full bar is a level-up.
glossary.where: Every kill drops one. Walk close and they fly to you.

glossary.name: Level-up
glossary.desc: The run stops and shows 3 cards: a new weapon or passive, or a level for one you carry. Pick one. Reroll draws new cards, Banish removes a card for the run, and Skip passes.
glossary.where: Each time the XP bar fills.

glossary.name: Weapon
glossary.desc: Fires on its own. Each level-up for it rolls a rarity: Common and Uncommon raise a number, Rare and Epic add a trait, Legendary a Legendary trait. It never runs out of levels.
glossary.more: Each weapon has tags and three Forms to choose. A run holds a few at once.
glossary.where: Every character starts with two: their signature weapon and a starting weapon. Level-ups offer more.

glossary.name: Passive
glossary.desc: A stat bonus you carry, such as more Damage (Fire) each level. It never fires. Its last level adds a bonus rule, shown on its card.
glossary.more: Some passives go with a weapon, and their card names it: each level gives that weapon's Final Form +6% Damage.
glossary.where: Level-ups. The Library's research adds more to the pool.

glossary.name: Tags
glossary.desc: Labels on weapons and passives: Light, Fire, Sea, Steel, Echo, Frost, and Rot. A passive with a tag boosts only weapons with that tag. A card's chips show how many of each tag you carry.
glossary.where: On every weapon and passive card.

glossary.name: Tag bonus
glossary.desc: A weapon gets +8% Damage for each other weapon or passive you carry that shares one of its tags, up to +24%.
glossary.where: Shown on a weapon's level-up card when it applies.

glossary.name: Wayside Lamp
glossary.desc: Stand in its circle until it lights; the Lamplighter lights one the moment she reaches it. A lit lamp stays lit, and its light burns enemies in it. Light every lamp on the map for a Lantern Night.
glossary.more: An ordinary enemy in its light dies in about 5s. A drop that lands in its light chimes. Lighting one pays Pearls once the Ferryman is in your runs.
glossary.short: Stay in its circle to light it; the Lamplighter lights one at a touch. It stays lit for the rest of the run, and its light burns enemies.
glossary.where: Each act brings 4 or 5 at new places. An arrow at the screen's edge points to the nearest.

glossary.name: Fog Bell
glossary.desc: Stand in its small circle to start it. A wave of enemies comes. Kill the number it asks, and it rings: it stuns enemies near it and leaves a chest that gives one weapon or passive +2 levels.
glossary.more: For the Tide Priest each bell rings twice: once rung, it can be started again for a bigger wave and a second chest.
glossary.short: Stand in its small circle to start it, then kill the wave that comes. It rings and leaves a chest.
glossary.where: Each act brings 3, one at a time at new places. An arrow at the screen's edge points to the nearest.

glossary.name: Chest
glossary.desc: Gives levels for a weapon or passive you carry, or Coin, or food. A boss chest gives 1, 3, or 5 things.
glossary.where: Elites and bosses drop them, and some map events leave one with guards (the chest arrow points to it). Walk over one to open it.

glossary.name: Ember
glossary.desc: Opens a weapon's next Form early, or swaps a Form it has for the other one of its pair. Use it when you pick it up, or later from the pause menu.
glossary.where: Bosses drop one, elites sometimes, and the Ferryman sells them.

glossary.name: Materials
glossary.desc: What runs bring home to restore buildings and pay for everything in the harbor. Each map drops its own, so what you need next says where to run.
glossary.where: Enemies drop them, and every minute of a run pays some. Iron and Map Scraps come mostly from elites and bosses. Salt Glass comes from the Salt Marsh's elites and its storm.

glossary.name: Restore
glossary.desc: Pay materials to bring a harbor building back. Each level does more: new things in your runs, or new things to buy.
glossary.where: Walk up to a building in the harbor.

glossary.name: Dash
glossary.desc: A quick burst of movement. Enemies can't hurt you during it. It has a short recharge. The Dash slot holds one dash item, which changes how the dash goes.
glossary.where: R1 or RB on a controller, Shift or Space on a keyboard. Settings, Controls changes the buttons.

glossary.name: Trait
glossary.desc: A weapon's Rare, Epic, or Legendary level-up: a named change to how that weapon works, such as flares that split. Each weapon has its own, and keeps them for the run.
glossary.more: A Shared trait can be rolled by more than one weapon, under one name; its card says Shared. Taking one changes only that weapon.
glossary.where: Rare and better level-up cards for a weapon you carry.

glossary.name: Burning
glossary.desc: A burning enemy takes fire damage every 0.25s until the fire goes out. A second fire doesn't add to the first: the stronger one stays.
glossary.where: Fire weapons, and traits and Forms that say they set enemies burning.

glossary.name: Slowed
glossary.desc: A slowed enemy moves slower, by the percent on the card. A stronger slow replaces a weaker one; they don't add.
glossary.where: Frost and Sea weapons, and traits and Forms that say they slow.

glossary.name: Frozen
glossary.desc: A frozen enemy can't move, but still hurts you if you touch it. A boss stays frozen 25% as long. Once it thaws it can't be frozen again for 2s.
glossary.where: Frost weapons, and traits and Forms that say they freeze.

glossary.name: Rotting
glossary.desc: A rotting enemy takes more damage from every hit while the rot lasts. The card says how much and for how long.
glossary.more: Some weapons make a rotting enemy burst, or rise to fight for the Bog Warden, when it dies.
glossary.where: Rot weapons, the Bog Warden, and traits and Forms that say they rot.

glossary.name: Stunned
glossary.desc: A stunned enemy can't move and can't hurt you by touch, for the time the card says. Bosses can't be stunned.
glossary.where: The Harpooner, and traits and Forms that say they stun.

glossary.name: Hooked
glossary.desc: A hooked enemy takes 25% more damage for 4s. The Harpooner's hook makes it 30% for 4s.
glossary.where: The Anchor Chain, the Harpooner's hook, and traits and skills that say they hook.

glossary.name: Finish
glossary.desc: Kills an enemy outright once its HP is under the percent on the card. Only ordinary enemies, not elites or bosses, unless the card says so.
glossary.where: The Drowned Man's Grave Pennies, and some Forms and traits.

glossary.name: Lost
glossary.desc: A lost enemy walks away from you for the time the card says, then comes back.
glossary.where: The Fog Horn and its traits and Forms.

glossary.name: Chain
glossary.desc: A hit that jumps on to nearby enemies, one after another. The card says how many.
glossary.where: The Lightning Rod, the Lantern Orb's Arc, and traits and passives that add Chain.

glossary.name: Pierce
glossary.desc: How many more enemies a shot passes through before it is spent. With none, a shot stops at the first enemy it hits.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats, and its Uncommon and better cards.

glossary.name: Crit
glossary.desc: Crit Chance is the chance a hit is a crit. A crit deals Crit Damage times the hit, and its number shows in gold.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats, and its Uncommon and better cards.

glossary.name: Hit Delay
glossary.desc: How long one enemy waits before the same weapon can hit it again. It matters most for weapons that stay out: orbits, beams, and pools.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats, and its Uncommon and better cards.

glossary.name: Knockback
glossary.desc: How far a hit pushes an enemy back.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats, and some traits and Forms.

glossary.name: Form
glossary.desc: A choice that changes how a weapon works. Each weapon picks three, one of two each time: at Lv 6, at Lv 11, and a Final Form when its goal is done.
glossary.more: Each Form shows its drawback. An Ember opens the next Form early, or swaps one. Some Final Forms also change how the weapon looks.
glossary.where: Leveling the weapon, its goal, or an Ember.

glossary.name: Final Form goal
glossary.desc: What opens a weapon's Final Form: something done with that weapon in the run, such as kills from far off. Each weapon has its own.
glossary.where: On its level-up cards and in the pause menu, and counted beside its icon in a run.

glossary.name: Signature weapon
glossary.desc: A character's own weapon. Nobody else can use it, and level-ups never offer it. It levels up every 3:00, and also from what the character does: lamps lit for the Lamplighter, sweeps for the Punter.
glossary.more: The meter under the weapons shows how close its next level is. Each lamp, sweep, or other count past what the next level needs adds +4% Damage, up to +40%.
glossary.where: Every character carries one, in the first weapon slot.

glossary.name: Drawback
glossary.desc: The rule against a character, or the cost of a Form. A character's is on their card at the gate; a Form's is on its card.
glossary.where: The gate's character cards, and every Form card.

glossary.name: Shield
glossary.desc: Soaks up damage before your HP does. Once it is gone, hits take HP again.
glossary.where: The Tide Priest's floods (her Tide Shield), and some relics.

glossary.name: Tide Shield
glossary.desc: The Tide Priest can't heal. Each flood leaves her a shield that soaks up damage, refilled only by her next flood. With it gone, she takes 15% more damage.
glossary.more: It holds 2 for each enemy the flood hit, at least 5 and up to 25, and 50% more for each Tide. The thin bar over her HP bar shows it.
glossary.where: The Tide Priest's runs.

glossary.name: Elite
glossary.desc: A bigger, tougher enemy that drops a chest. Its name, and any elite powers, show when it arrives.
glossary.where: On the map's timeline, and more often at higher Tides.

glossary.name: Elite powers
glossary.desc: An extra rule an elite carries, named when it arrives: Shielded, Herald, Molten, Tethered, or Brine. Each has its own entry here.
glossary.where: One on every elite, two from Tide 2. A muster's captain has none.

glossary.name: Shielded
glossary.desc: Its shield takes 3 hits to break. Until then the elite takes no damage.
glossary.where: An elite power.

glossary.name: Herald
glossary.desc: Comes with 6 of its own kind.
glossary.where: An elite power.

glossary.name: Molten
glossary.desc: Leaves burning ground where it walks.
glossary.where: An elite power.

glossary.name: Tethered
glossary.desc: Linked to 2 of its own kind. While they live, they share the damage it takes.
glossary.where: An elite power.

glossary.name: Brine (elite)
glossary.desc: Its touch slows you by 30% for 2s.
glossary.where: An elite power.

glossary.name: Boss phases
glossary.desc: The marks on a boss's HP bar. A boss can't lose HP past a mark until it has used that phase's big attack once.
glossary.more: While a boss is stuck in mud or kneeling, hits land in full.
glossary.where: Every boss.

glossary.name: Muster
glossary.desc: A captain and a ring of crew that walk in together. Kill the captain for a chest. Some captains have one attack of their own, shown by a ring on the ground first.
glossary.more: The 5:00 captain drops an elite's chest, the 17:30 one a boss chest and an Ember. The Salt Marsh's 17:30 captain comes once you have cleared the Marsh.
glossary.where: At set times on every map. In overtime they keep coming, and a line says when one is 5s away.

glossary.name: Boss
glossary.desc: A big enemy with its own attacks, each shown on the ground before it lands. Each drops a boss chest and an Ember.
glossary.where: At 10:00 and 20:00 on every map.

glossary.name: Overtime
glossary.desc: After the last boss you can stay. Enemies get stronger every minute and drop more materials. The map stays cleared whatever happens.
glossary.more: New lamps and bells come out, the first boss comes back at 5:00, and at 10:00 the Long Night starts.
glossary.where: The question after the 20:00 boss. Quit run from the pause menu ends it.

glossary.name: Act
glossary.desc: One of a run's three parts. Each act brings its own Wayside Lamps and Fog Bells at new places. Lamps you lit stay lit.
glossary.more: From Act 2 an act can bring a twist: a slow lamp, or a bell whose wave an elite leads. Act 3 is overtime.
glossary.where: Act 1 from the start, Act 2 when the first boss comes, Act 3 in overtime.

glossary.name: Long Night
glossary.desc: The end of overtime. The map's bosses come back together. Kill them all and dawn breaks. If they kill you first, the run ends (the map stays cleared).
glossary.where: Overtime, 10 minutes after you stay.

glossary.name: Dawn
glossary.desc: The Long Night is won. The last enemies fall, every chest and Ember on the ground comes to you, a boss chest opens, and the run ends.
glossary.where: Kill every boss of the Long Night.

glossary.name: Momentum
glossary.desc: The Punter's meter. It fills while he keeps moving. A sharp turn costs a step, a hit costs 50% of it, and stopping empties it. Each of its 4 steps adds 10% Damage, and +4% Area to his Punt Pole.
glossary.more: At full Momentum his Punt Pole sweeps all around him every 3s. With none his weapons deal 25% less damage.
glossary.short: The Punter's meter: it fills while he moves, and each step is more Damage.
glossary.where: The Punter's runs, the bar at his feet.

glossary.name: Fuel
glossary.desc: The Lamplighter's light runs on Fuel. Away from lit lamps it lasts 60s, then her light dims over 30s, down to 60% of its Area and Damage, and her Pickup Range too. A lit lamp refills it.
glossary.where: The Lamplighter's runs: the Fuel bar at the top left.

glossary.name: Spare flame
glossary.desc: The Lamplighter holds up to 3. Each gives her light +15% Damage and +15% Area moving (+5% standing). She gains one every 5s with 5 or more enemies in her light, and all at once by lighting a lamp.
glossary.short: The Lamplighter's flames: each one held makes her light bigger and deal more damage.
glossary.where: The Lamplighter's runs: the pips beside Spare flames, top left.

glossary.name: Lamplighter's lantern
glossary.desc: A small light the Lamplighter sets down: one by each lamp she lights, and one every 30s while her light is dimmed. It lasts 60s, burns enemies in it at 60% of Lamplight's damage, and gives Lamplight +10% Damage.
glossary.where: The Lamplighter's runs.

glossary.name: Grave penny
glossary.desc: What the Drowned Man's purse holds. A penny that lands close to him puts one in, and so do his weapons' finishing hits close by. A full purse of 24 marks a sunken crate nearby.
glossary.short: The Drowned Man's purse: a full one marks a sunken crate nearby.
glossary.where: The Drowned Man's runs.

glossary.name: Relic
glossary.desc: Changes a rule for the rest of the run (gems that explode, a shield instead of healing). Relics come in 3 rarities: Common, Uncommon, and Rare. They never show on level-up cards.
glossary.where: Reliquaries, the vault, the Ferryman, and secrets.

glossary.name: Relic slots
glossary.desc: How many relics a run can carry. With them full, a new relic means giving up one you carry (the Ferryman sells it again), or passing.
glossary.where: A run starts with 3. The Docks' Lv 3, Lv 4, and Lv 5 each add one, up to 6.

glossary.name: Weapon and passive slots
glossary.desc: How many weapons and passives a run can carry. Once they are full, level-ups offer levels for what you carry. Weapons never run out of levels.
glossary.where: A run starts with 4 weapon slots and 4 passive slots. The Lamp Post's Lv 3 and Lv 5 each add a weapon slot, up to 6. The Smithy's Lv 2 and Lv 4 each add a passive slot, up to 6.

glossary.name: Dash item
glossary.desc: Changes how the dash goes: how far, how often, how many charges, and what the ground does where you dashed. A run holds one. A level-up can offer another in its place.
glossary.where: Every character starts with one. Level-ups offer the others.

glossary.name: Pearls
glossary.desc: Money for the Ferryman, spent in the same run. Pearls left at the end are lost, unless the Market buys them as Coin.
glossary.where: Lit lamps, rung bells, and elites pay them, once the Docks bring the Ferryman.

glossary.name: Food
glossary.desc: Heals you. The Tide Priest can't heal, so none drops in her runs.
glossary.where: Dropped by enemies now and then, in chests, and sold by the Ferryman.

glossary.name: Reroll
glossary.desc: Draws 3 new level-up cards. Each run has a few.
glossary.where: Every run starts with 2. The Apothecary and the Ferryman sell more.

glossary.name: Banish
glossary.desc: Takes one level-up card out of the run for good. On a weapon's level-up, it takes that kind of level-up off that weapon.
glossary.where: Every run starts with 2. The Apothecary sells more.

glossary.name: Skip
glossary.desc: Passes a level-up without taking a card. Hold it so it can't happen by accident. A skip pays a little: food when you are hurt, else Pearls or Coin.
glossary.where: Every run starts with 2. The Apothecary sells more.

glossary.name: Revival
glossary.desc: Brings you back once at 50% HP when you would die.
glossary.where: Smelling Salts at the Apothecary, and the Lamp Post's last Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: Rarity
glossary.desc: How good something is, lowest to highest: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, and Legendary. The word always shows with its color. A higher rarity is a bigger number, or a trait.
glossary.more: A weapon's Legendary trait comes only at Legendary. Gear goes up one rarity each time the Smithy improves it, and at Rare gains one more bonus.
glossary.where: Weapon level-ups, relics, and gear at the Smithy.

glossary.name: Luck
glossary.desc: Makes good rolls likelier: higher rarities on level-ups, more in a boss chest, Reliquaries, food, and drops.
glossary.where: Passives, relics, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: Damage
glossary.desc: How much each hit takes off an enemy. A +% Damage card raises it by that percent.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.
glossary.more: Each Damage card on the same weapon adds 16% less than the last. The card's numbers already show it.

glossary.name: Area
glossary.desc: How big a weapon's hits, rings, and pools are.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.

glossary.name: Cooldown
glossary.desc: How long a weapon waits between attacks. Lower is faster.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.

glossary.name: Duration
glossary.desc: How long a weapon's effects last: pools, beams, orbits, statuses.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.

glossary.name: Projectiles
glossary.desc: How many shots a weapon fires at once. A card may use the weapon's own word, such as flares.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.

glossary.name: Projectile Speed
glossary.desc: How fast a weapon's shots fly.
glossary.where: A weapon's stats in the pause menu, and level-up cards.

glossary.name: Range
glossary.desc: How far from you a weapon reaches: how far a shot or hook flies, or how far out it swings. Area is how big each hit is.
glossary.where: Some Forms and skills: Muzzle Flash, Short Hook, Long Chain, Breathing Ring, and Hand Line.

glossary.name: Armor
glossary.desc: Takes this much off every hit you take.
glossary.where: Your stats in the pause menu (Stats), passive and relic cards, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: HP Regen
glossary.desc: HP you get back each second.
glossary.where: Your stats in the pause menu (Stats), passive and relic cards, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: Move Speed
glossary.desc: How fast you walk.
glossary.where: Your stats in the pause menu (Stats), passive and relic cards, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: Pickup Range
glossary.desc: How close a gem or drop must be before it flies to you.
glossary.where: Your stats in the pause menu (Stats), passive and relic cards, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: XP Gain
glossary.desc: More XP from every gem.
glossary.where: Your stats in the pause menu (Stats), passive and relic cards, gear, and Harbor upgrades.

glossary.name: Light tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Lamps, flares, beams, and lightning. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Fire tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Weapons that set enemies burning. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Sea tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Water, waves, and things from the sea. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Steel tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Heavy hooks, chains, and anchors. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Echo tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Sound: bells and horns. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Frost tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Weapons that slow and freeze. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Rot tag
glossary.desc: A tag. Weapons that make enemies rot. A passive with this tag boosts only weapons with it.
glossary.where: The chips on weapon and passive cards.

glossary.name: Slow lamp
glossary.desc: A Wayside Lamp that takes longer to light, while enemies rush it. Once lit, it works like any other lamp, plus a chest and twice the Pearls.
glossary.where: A twist an act can bring, from Act 2.

glossary.name: Lantern Night
glossary.desc: The fog lifts for 40s and your light burns every enemy near you. When it ends, a vault rises ahead of you. Once ready, it starts when 15 enemies are near you, or a muster or boss arrives.
glossary.more: The Lamplighter earns 2 at once, hers start with 10 enemies near, and her light reaches farther.
glossary.where: Light every Wayside Lamp on the map. Each act brings new lamps, so you can earn it again.

glossary.name: Vault
glossary.desc: Pick one relic of 3, one rarity higher than a Reliquary's.
glossary.where: Rises ahead of you when Lantern Night ends.

glossary.name: Crane
glossary.desc: Stand in the circle at its foot until it fills. It drops 3 loads on the biggest crowd near it. A ring shows where each lands, and none can hurt you. Ready again each act.
glossary.where: The Drowned Docks: 4, in the Crane Yard, on the Breakwater quay, and by the Dry Dock.

glossary.name: Salt Cairn
glossary.desc: Stand in the circle at its foot until it fills. For 20s lightning strikes the biggest crowds near it. A ring shows where each lands, and none can hurt you. Ready again each act.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh: 4 on the flats.

glossary.name: Map event
glossary.desc: Something that happens on the map in an act: gulls, a ghost ship, a guarded chest, a trail of gems to a chest. Each run draws a few for each act.
glossary.where: Every map has its own. Harbor Orders open more of them.

glossary.name: Reliquary
glossary.desc: Walk over it to pick one relic of 3. It lasts for the rest of the run.
glossary.short: A rare drop from a kill. Walk over it to pick one relic of 3.
glossary.where: A rare drop from kills. If 500 kills pass without one, the next kill drops one.

glossary.name: Ferryman
glossary.desc: Rows in every few minutes and ties up near you. Stand in the circle by his boat to buy relics, food, rerolls, and Embers with Pearls.
glossary.short: He rows in every few minutes and ties up near you. Stand in the circle by his boat to buy relics, food, rerolls, and Embers with Pearls.
glossary.where: In every run once the Docks are restored, first at 3:00, then every 5 minutes.

glossary.name: Salt Well
glossary.desc: Give up one relic you carry. It's gone for the run, and from then on the Ferryman sells it on every map. To be asked again, stand still in its circle.
glossary.short: Give up one relic here. The Ferryman sells it on every map after.
glossary.where: On the Salt Marsh after your first clear there, where the 17:30 muster's captain falls.

glossary.name: Secret
glossary.desc: A hidden place at a map's edge. The big one holds a relic that then joins the pool for good. Small secrets give Pearls, an Ember, an item, materials, or food once a run.
glossary.more: A small one shows only as a faint glint when you are close. Walk onto it. The Salt Marsh's big one is on the Drowned Causeway, and only the Bog Warden finds anything there.
glossary.where: At the edges of each map: one big one and 5 or 6 small ones. The Cartographer gives hints.

glossary.name: District
glossary.desc: A named part of a map: the Drowned Docks have the Crane Yard, the Fish Market, the Breakwater, the Ropewalk, the Dry Dock, and the Wreck. Notices name them.
glossary.where: The Drowned Docks and the Salt Marsh.

glossary.name: High water
glossary.desc: The Salt Marsh's creeks flood twice a run, and nobody can walk through them. A warning comes 15s ahead. The way back to the landing never floods.
glossary.short: The creeks flood twice a run and close. Only the Punter and enemies that swim cross them.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh, 3:00 to 8:00 and 13:00 to 18:00.

glossary.name: Herb beds
glossary.desc: Beds of Marsh Herbs on the creek mud. Walk over one to pick it. High water covers them.
glossary.short: Marsh Herbs on the creek mud. Walk over them at low water.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh's creeks, at low water.

glossary.name: Drowned Causeway
glossary.desc: A stone path to an island in the far southeast of the Salt Marsh, dry at low water. Only the Bog Warden can raise the dead there; for anyone else it is empty.
glossary.short: A stone path to an island in the far southeast, dry at low water. Only the Bog Warden finds anything there.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh, once its second Tide is open or the Cartographer is fully restored.

glossary.name: Mooring post
glossary.desc: Where the Ferryman ties up. As the Harpooner, stand in a post's circle until it fills and he rows to that post now. Once each time he comes.
glossary.where: Along the water on every map with the Ferryman.

glossary.name: Floating chest
glossary.desc: A chest floating on the water. Only the Punter can get to it, by crossing the water: a crossing lasts 5s, then the water carries him to a bank, slowed for 3s. It holds one item.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh: one each high water. The Drowned Docks: one in the slips each act.

glossary.name: Bog body
glossary.desc: A body kept in the marsh peat. As the Bog Warden, walk into its circle: it rises and fights for her for 40s. Once a run each.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh: 6 in the peat.

glossary.name: Wreck crew
glossary.desc: A drowned crew where their boat went down. As the Bog Warden, walk into its circle: 4 of them rise and fight for her for 30s. Once a run each.
glossary.where: The Drowned Docks: 5, by the Wreck, the Dry Dock, and on the wharf.

glossary.name: Thrall
glossary.desc: A dead enemy that got up to fight for the Bog Warden, for 6s. She can have 6 at once. They go for the enemy nearest her, and a bite stuns an ordinary enemy for 0.4s.
glossary.short: A dead enemy that got up to fight for the Bog Warden for 6s.
glossary.where: The Bog Warden's runs: enemies that die rotting, die in her Bog Hands, or that she walks over just after they die.

glossary.name: Sunken crate
glossary.desc: Cargo on the sea floor. As the Drowned Man, walk into its circle and he brings it up: one item. A full purse of 24 pennies marks one nearby.
glossary.where: Every map has 7 or 8.

glossary.name: Sea chest
glossary.desc: Every 3rd crate the Drowned Man brings up. The first gives back 1 of his 2 missing weapon slots, with a weapon in it. Later ones give Grave Pennies 1 level.
glossary.where: The Drowned Man's runs.

glossary.name: Storm
glossary.desc: Lightning falls on the biggest crowd on the salt flats. A ring on the ground shows where first. Every 8th strike leaves Salt Glass, and a strike on salt can raise a glass pillar.
glossary.short: Lightning falls on the biggest crowd on the salt flats. A ring on the ground shows where first.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh, once you have killed the Old Grey.

glossary.name: Eye of the storm
glossary.desc: For 45s no enemies come, and heavier lightning falls on the ones left. It leaves gems and 4 Salt Glass.
glossary.short: No enemies come for a while, and heavier lightning falls on the ones left.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh at 19:00, once the storm comes.

glossary.name: Glass pillar
glossary.desc: Glass that lightning raises where it strikes salt. It stands for 8s, and nothing walks through it, you included.
glossary.short: Lightning on salt raises one for 8s. Nothing walks through it.
glossary.where: The Salt Marsh's salt flats, in the storm.

glossary.name: Tide
glossary.desc: A harder version of a map for more materials: tougher, faster enemies, and more of them. From Tide 2 each Tide also adds a rule, and keeps the ones below it.
glossary.short: A harder version of the map that pays more materials.
glossary.where: Kill a map's last boss to open its Tide 1, then clear each Tide to open the next. Pick one at the gate once the Chapel is restored.

glossary.name: Curse
glossary.desc: One rule against you for a run (less Max HP, more enemies, no food) for more materials. They stack.
glossary.where: The Chapel opens them. Pick them at the gate.

glossary.name: Heirloom
glossary.desc: One relic you have found before, carried from the start of a run. It takes a relic slot.
glossary.short: One relic you have found before, carried from the start of a run. It takes a relic slot.
glossary.where: The Tavern opens it at level 3. Pick it at the gate.

glossary.name: Run tool
glossary.desc: Something for one run: rerolls, banishes, skips, a Revival, or a head start (Pearls or an Ember). The run uses it up.
glossary.short: Something for one run: rerolls, banishes, skips, a Revival, or a head start. The run uses it up.
glossary.where: Bought at the Apothecary, picked at the gate under Run tools.

glossary.name: Research
glossary.desc: Pay materials to start a project. It finishes after a few runs, and what it finds can then turn up in your runs. A run counts if you survive 5:00 or kill a boss.
glossary.more: The Library's levels open more projects. A project that finds things for a building needs that building restored first.
glossary.short: Pay materials to start a project, and it finishes after a few runs.
glossary.where: The Library.

glossary.name: Harbor upgrades
glossary.desc: Small bonuses for every run, such as more Damage each rank. Each has a few ranks.
glossary.where: Bought at the Lamp Post. Its levels open more.

glossary.name: Gear
glossary.desc: Pieces you wear into every run (lantern, coat, boots, keepsake, ring, and pendant), each with bonuses. The Smithy improves gear up to Legendary and rerolls its bonuses.
glossary.where: Made at the Smithy from patterns. Harbor Orders, the Library's research, mastery, and the Lighthouse open them.

glossary.name: Harbor Orders
glossary.desc: Goals the townsfolk post: kill a boss with a certain weapon, light lamps, clear a map at a Tide. Each opens one new thing when you get home. Challenge runs and Hunts are orders too.
glossary.more: What they open: gear, a trophy, a starting weapon, a skill, something in the harbor, a map event, a relic, a run tool, a character, a weapon, or a passive. A Hunt is an order to kill a set number of one enemy, counting every run; it opens +5% Damage against that enemy.
glossary.short: Goals the townsfolk post. Each opens one new thing when you get home.
glossary.where: The board at the Tavern. Orders count from your first run; the board shows them once the Tavern is restored.

glossary.name: Starting weapon
glossary.desc: The weapon a character starts a run with, beside their signature weapon. Other starting weapons can be picked at the gate.
glossary.where: Mastery ranks 2 and 4 open a character's own, and weapon orders on the Harbor Orders board open one for everyone.

glossary.name: Mastery
glossary.desc: Each character earns ranks as you play them. Ranks give skill points, and open starting weapons, gear, and a challenge run of their own.
glossary.short: A character earns ranks as you play them. Ranks give skill points to spend at the Tavern, and open starting weapons, gear, and a challenge run.
glossary.where: The Tavern, from its level 2.

glossary.name: Skills
glossary.desc: Each character has a tree of 13 skills and 7 points for it, from mastery ranks. A skill changes their signature weapon, what they do on the map, or their drawback.
glossary.more: Some skills close another, some need another first, and two in each tree open with a Harbor Order. A tree can be reset for materials.
glossary.short: Each character has a skill tree. Mastery ranks give points for it, and there are never enough for the whole tree.
glossary.where: The Tavern, from its level 2: the Mastery list.

glossary.name: Codex
glossary.desc: What you have found: every weapon, passive, relic, enemy, boss, map, and secret, with blanks for the ones not seen. An enemy's page counts your kills; a weapon's shows its Forms and traits.
glossary.short: What you have found, with blanks for what you have not. An enemy's page counts your kills.
glossary.where: The Library once it is restored, the harbor's menu, and the pause menu in a run.

glossary.name: Completion
glossary.desc: How much of the game you have done, as a percent: buildings, research, the codex, Harbor Orders, Tides, and mastery.
glossary.where: The title screen.

glossary.name: Challenge run
glossary.desc: A Harbor Order with its own rules: a set character, map, Tide, and curses. Start it from the board.
glossary.short: A Harbor Order with its own rules: a set character, map, Tide, and curses.
glossary.where: The Cartographer posts them from its level 3. Start one from the Harbor Orders board at the Tavern.

glossary.name: Short run
glossary.desc: Everything comes twice as fast, the last boss comes at 10:00, and the run pays 40% of the materials.
glossary.short: Everything comes twice as fast, the last boss comes at 10:00, and the run pays 40% of the materials.
glossary.where: The Cartographer opens it. Pick it at the gate under Map.

glossary.name: Next up
glossary.desc: The three things in the harbor you can nearly afford, with how close each is. Ready means you can buy it now.
glossary.where: The bottom left of the harbor, and the results after a run.

glossary.name: Save code
glossary.desc: Your progress as text, to keep as a backup or move to the other build of the game.
glossary.where: The title's menu and the harbor's menu.

glossary.name: Lamp Post
glossary.desc: The harbor's big lamp. Each level pushes the fog back and opens new Harbor upgrades, bought here with materials, for every run. Two of its levels add a weapon slot to your runs.
glossary.where: Restore it with Oil and Coin. It stands on the square.

glossary.name: Library
glossary.desc: Pay materials to start a research project. It finishes after a few runs, and what it finds (new weapons, passives, and relics) can then turn up in your runs.
glossary.where: Restore it with Drowned Pages, Coin, and Timber.

glossary.name: Tavern
glossary.desc: Keeps the Harbor Orders board (goals the townsfolk post) and each character's mastery. Its later levels add relics to your runs and let a run set out with an Heirloom.
glossary.where: Restore it with Coin, Rum, and Timber.

glossary.name: Docks
glossary.desc: Restore the Docks and the Ferryman appears in your runs, tying up near you to sell relics, food, and more for Pearls. Each level improves what he sells, and its later levels add relic slots.
glossary.where: Restore it with Timber, Rope, and Coin.

glossary.name: Smithy
glossary.desc: Make gear here: pieces you wear into every run, each with a bonus. Its levels add passive slots to your runs. A later level gives your starting weapon one of its Rare traits in every run.
glossary.where: Restore it with Iron, Timber, and Coin. The fog clears from it at the Lamp Post's Lv 4.

glossary.name: Chapel
glossary.desc: Opens Tides, then curses: ways to make a run harder for more materials. You pick them at the gate before a run.
glossary.where: Restore it with Drowned Pages, Oil, and Coin. The fog clears from it at the Lamp Post's Lv 3.

glossary.name: Market
glossary.desc: Swap a material you have plenty of for one you need, at a poor rate. Later, Pearls you didn't spend in a run come home as Coin.
glossary.where: Restore it with Coin and Timber.

glossary.name: Apothecary
glossary.desc: Sells run tools: rerolls, banishes, skips, a Revival, and a head start for one run. You pick them at the gate, and the run uses them up. Its other levels make food heal more.
glossary.where: Restore it with Rum, Oil, and Coin. Its later levels take Marsh Herbs from the Salt Marsh.

glossary.name: Cartographer
glossary.desc: Draws more onto your minimap: Reliquaries wherever they drop, then small secrets, then the big ones, with hints. It also posts Challenge runs on the Harbor Orders board and opens short runs.
glossary.where: Restore it with Map Scraps, Drowned Pages, and Coin.

glossary.name: Lighthouse
glossary.desc: The old light on the point. Relight it stage by stage with materials from every map. Each stage shows on the tower and opens something new. The last stage lights the lamp.
glossary.more: A stage opens gear, a run tool, a relic, a challenge run, faster Wayside Lamps (stage 1), one more run tool a run (stage 4), wider Fog Bell circles (stage 8), or more Iron and Map Scraps at the Market (stage 7).
glossary.where: East of the Market. The fog clears from it with the Lamp Post's last level.

glossary.name: Gate
glossary.desc: Where runs start: choose the map, the character, and what the harbor has opened: a starting weapon, an Heirloom, run tools, and how hard (a Tide and curses).
glossary.where: The west end of the quay. Walking off the quay opens it too.
